title: Ensure 'Create symbolic links' is set to 'Administrators, NT VIRTUAL MACHINE\Virtual Machines' (MS only)
objective: Audit CIS checkpoint 2.2.18 on Windows Server 2022: verify the 'Create symbolic links' user right (SeCreateSymbolicLinkPrivilege) is assigned to Administrators (S-1-5-32-544), plus NT VIRTUAL MACHINE\Virtual Machines (S-1-5-83-0) only when Hyper-V is installed, correctly handling domain controller hosts where Hyper-V is unsupported and the right may be delivered by a Domain Controllers GPO.

playbook_input.description: Parameters the caller provides before execution

steps.name: Detect host role (domain controller vs member server) and Hyper-V state
steps.function: 1. Determine the host role (domain controller vs member/standalone server) and whether the Hyper-V role is installed: `powershell -Command "$cs = Get-CimInstance Win32_ComputerSystem; Write-Output ('DomainRole=' + $cs.DomainRole); Write-Output ('HyperV=' + (Get-WindowsFeature -Name Hyper-V).InstallState)"`. Expected: DomainRole 4 (Backup DC) or 5 (Primary DC) indicates a domain controller; 3 indicates a member server; HyperV='Installed' means the Hyper-V role is present, 'Available'/'Removed' means it is not.

steps.name: Check the 'Create symbolic links' user right assignment
steps.function: 2. Export effective user rights and read the 'Create symbolic links' assignment: `secedit /export /areas USER_RIGHTS /cfg $env:TEMP\secpol_export.inf; Select-String -Path $env:TEMP\secpol_export.inf -Pattern 'SeCreateSymbolicLinkPrivilege'`. Expected: 'SeCreateSymbolicLinkPrivilege = *S-1-5-32-544,*S-1-5-83-0' (Administrators and NT VIRTUAL MACHINE\Virtual Machines) when Hyper-V is installed; 'SeCreateSymbolicLinkPrivilege = *S-1-5-32-544' (Administrators only) on a domain controller and on any host without Hyper-V. Any additional account or group SID is a FAIL.

steps.name: Check the 'Create symbolic links' policy via registry
steps.function: 3. Check for a policy-driven value: `reg query "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System" /v CreateSymbolicLink`. Expected: this value is usually absent on a domain controller because the right is stored in the security database and applied by GPO rather than through this key; absence is normal and is not by itself a FAIL. If present, its SID list must match Administrators (plus NT VIRTUAL MACHINE\Virtual Machines only when Hyper-V is installed).

steps.name: Identify policy source (local policy vs Domain Controllers GPO)
steps.function: 4. On a domain controller, determine whether the assignment is delivered by a domain GPO rather than local policy: `powershell -Command "Import-Module GroupPolicy -ErrorAction Stop; $p = Join-Path $env:TEMP 'gpo_report.xml'; Get-GPOReport -All -ReportType Xml -Path $p; Select-String -Path $p -Pattern 'SeCreateSymbolicLinkPrivilege'"`. Expected: any GPO granting the right to principals beyond Administrators (and NT VIRTUAL MACHINE\Virtual Machines when Hyper-V is installed) is a FAIL; no match means the local/default assignment applies. If the GroupPolicy module is unavailable (member server without RSAT, or command failure), report SKIP for the policy-source check only and rely on the secedit output from step-02.

steps.name: Summarize overall compliance status: PASS if the 'Create symbolic links' user right is assigned to Administrators and…
steps.function: 5. Summarize overall compliance status: PASS if the 'Create symbolic links' user right is assigned exactly to Administrators, plus NT VIRTUAL MACHINE\Virtual Machines when Hyper-V is Installed; SKIP if the audit cannot be performed due to missing prerequisites (host role/Hyper-V state undeterminable, secedit unavailable, insufficient privileges); FAIL if the right is assigned to unauthorized accounts or missing required principals.

computations._cis_status: FAIL if SeCreateSymbolicLinkPrivilege is assigned to any principal other than Administrators (S-1-5-32-544) and, when Hyper-V is Installed, NT VIRTUAL MACHINE\Virtual Machines (S-1-5-83-0); PASS if it is assigned to Administrators only on a domain controller or a host without Hyper-V, or to Administrators plus S-1-5-83-0 when Hyper-V is Installed; SKIP if host role or Hyper-V state cannot be determined or secedit output is unavailable

steps.name: Store the final audit result in a variable named 'cis_result' using set_fact. Set cis_result to the overall compliance…
steps.function: 6. Store the final audit result in a variable named 'cis_result' using set_fact. Set cis_result to the overall compliance status (PASS/FAIL/SKIP/ERROR) derived from the last requirement's status variable.

compliance_constraints: Use failed_when: false on all audit tasks (except set_fact, debug) so all checks complete and report status
If the audit targets a specific software/service (e.g., GDM, GNOME, sshd, httpd), FIRST check if it is installed. If NOT installed, report SKIP for all checks.
This is an AUDIT playbook — it MUST NOT make any changes to the system. All tasks must be read-only (shell commands, stat, slurp, command with check-only flags, etc.).

On a domain controller (Win32_ComputerSystem DomainRole 4 or 5), Hyper-V is not a supported role: expect 'SeCreateSymbolicLinkPrivilege = *S-1-5-32-544' (Administrators only). Do NOT FAIL on a domain controller solely because NT VIRTUAL MACHINE\Virtual Machines (S-1-5-83-0) is absent.

On a domain controller, user rights may be delivered by a Domain Controllers GPO rather than local policy. Report the source (local policy vs GPO) in the audit details; if the effective assignment cannot be determined because the GroupPolicy module/RSAT is unavailable, report SKIP rather than FAIL.
